title: Existence of a generating sequence whose successive quotients are the residue field at a minimal prime of the support of a finite module
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For a finite module M over a local Noetherian ring R and a prime q that is a minimal prime of the support of M, the lemma produces elements x_1, ..., x_l of M such that the support of M/<x_1, ..., x_l> misses q while each successive quotient <x_1, ..., x_i>/<x_1, ..., x_{i-1}> is isomorphic to R/q, and it adds that necessarily l = length_{R_q}(M_q) (statement lines 17963-17977). The proof is a clearing-of-denominators argument rather than a citation: it takes a chain y_1, ..., y_l in the localisation M_q with the required successive quotients, lifts f_i y_i to elements z_i of M with f_i not in q, writes q = (g_1, ..., g_t) by Noetherianity, records that g_j y_i lies in <y_1, ..., y_{i-1}> after localising, and clears the finitely many denominators f_{ij} not in q to get f_{ij} g_j z_i in <z_1, ..., z_{i-1}> inside M; the products of the f's times z_i then have the required property because all cleared scalars are invertible at q, and each quotient is a one-generator R-module annihilated by q whose localisation at q is one dimensional over kappa(q), hence is R/q (proof lines 17980-18013). That last identification and the length statement are the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.
